title: DBS microelectrode recordings from 132 patients, University Clinical Centre Gdańsk (Osowska, Szymański, Libionka 2026; derivative: authors' band-passed, classifier-selected MER segments)
description: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings (MER) from 132 patients undergoing deep brain stimulation surgery at the University Clinical Centre in Gdańsk, Poland. Patients had Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, dystonia, tremor or epilepsy. This derivative contains short, band-pass filtered segments selected by a signal-quality classifier, recorded with up to five parallel electrodes at successive depths relative to the planned target. It includes 29 expert-annotated excerpts labelled as striatum/putamen, GPe or GPi, and is repackaged in BIDS (BrainVision format).
methods_description: Recordings were acquired during awake DBS surgery under local anaesthesia with an inomed ISIS MER system and up to five parallel MicroMacro electrodes in a Ben-gun configuration, sampled at 20 kHz. Signals were band-pass filtered at 500-5000 Hz (4th-order Butterworth) and clipped. A Random Forest classifier on 0.5 s windows (neuronal activity, background, artifact) selected the longest usable fragment per depth recording.
